review_comments.body: is this true that all the exporters in this package have two copies to truncate?

Not exactly: two copies is an upper bound, not what every built-in exporter does. Only the exporters with an `OperationsFormat` option (EventBridge, File, Firehose, Http, OTel, SQS) can render `BOTH` (the operations array plus the by-name map), which is the case that needs the bound of 2; OTel additionally embeds the rendered JSON once as a string body. Exporters such as CloudWatchLogs, DynamoDB, S3, OpenSearch, Aurora and Redshift render a single copy, so for them 2 is merely conservative: it can drop an operation or two earlier than strictly needed, never later, so the size limit still holds.

I kept one shared bound so the check is the same for every built-in exporter and `BOTH` drops the same operations as measuring each step. If you would rather have it exact, I can make the copy count a property of the exporter (for example a default method on `TelemetryExporter` that the format-aware exporters override) and drop the package-name check. Happy to do that here if you prefer.
